did_you_know.text: The verse names both Eleazar the priest and Joshua — showing a mix of religious and military authority in charge of dividing the land.
The Levites did not receive a territorial agricultural inheritance like the other tribes; their role was to receive cities and pasture plots so they could serve the sanctuary.
Caleb is called 'the Kenizzite' — a designation that points to a link with the Kenizzite group mentioned elsewhere in the Bible.
At eighty-five Caleb says 'the LORD has kept me alive' and that his strength is as in his younger days — in the Bible long life combined with vigor is often seen as a sign of divine blessing.
Hebron was formerly called 'Kiriath Arba' and in the text linked to the Anakim; later biblical books present it as an important city — for example, David's first residence.
